text: The stereoisomers that are formed by electrophilic addition of bromine to trans-but-2-ene is/are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Bromine adds to an alkene through a cyclic bromonium ion, which $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ opens from the opposite face, so the two Br atoms add anti.

Anti addition to trans-but-2-ene gives (2R,3S)-2,3-dibromobutane, which has a plane of symmetry and is the meso compound.

Attack of $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ at either carbon of the bromonium ion, and bromonium formation on either face of the alkene, lead to this same meso compound; no enantiomers are formed. The products are therefore two identical meso forms.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: The potassium ferrocyanide solution gives a Prussian blue colour, when added to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Potassium ferrocyanide supplies the hexacyanidoferrate(II) ion, $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{4-}$. With $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ ions it forms insoluble iron(III) hexacyanidoferrate(II), Prussian blue, in which $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ takes the place of $\mathrm{K}{}^{+}$ as the outer cation:

$4~\mathrm{FeCl}{}_{3}+3\mathrm{K}{}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]\longrightarrow \mathrm{Fe}{}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}_{3}+12\mathrm{KCl}$

With $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ (from $\mathrm{FeCl}{}_{2}$) only a white precipitate of $\mathrm{K}{}_{2}\mathrm{Fe}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]$ forms, and cobalt salts give no blue colour.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text:
Number of paramagnetic oxides among the following given oxides is $____________$.

$Li_{2}O$, CaO, $Na_{2}O_{2}, KO_{2}$, MgO and $K_{2}O$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$Li_{2}O$ $\Rightarrow$ $2Li^{+} O^{2-}$

CaO $\Rightarrow$ $Ca^{2+} O^{2-}$

$Na_{2}O_{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ $2Na^{+} O{}_{2}^{2-}$

$KO_{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ O${}_{2}^{-}$

MgO $\Rightarrow$ $Mg^{2+} O^{2-}$

$K_{2}O$ $\Rightarrow$ $2K^{+} O^{2-}$

$O^{2-}$ $\Rightarrow$ Complete octet, diamagnetic

$O_{2}^{2-}$ has 18 electrons.

Molecular orbital configuration of $O_{2}^{2-}$ is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}^{\ast }$

There is no unpaired electron so it is diamagnetic.

$O_{2}^{-}$ has 17 electrons.

Molecular orbital configuration of $O_{2}^{-}$ is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{1}}^{\ast }$

There is 1 unpaired electron so it is paramagnetic.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: For the reaction, $2NO_{2}(g)$ $⇌$ $N_{2}O_{4}(g)$, when $\Delta$S = $-176.0 JK^{-1}$ and $\Delta$H = $-$57.8 kJ mol$^{-1}$, the magnitude of $\Delta$G at 298 K for the reaction is $___________ kJ$ mol$^{-1}. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $\Delta$H = $-$ 57.8 kJ mol$^{-1}$

$\Delta$S = $-$ $176 JK^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$

T = 298 K

Using Gibb's free energy relation

$\Delta$G = $\Delta$H $-$ T$\Delta$S

where, $\Delta$G = change in Gibb's free energy

$\Delta$H = change in enthalpy

T = temperature

$\Delta$S = change in entropy

$\Delta$G = $-$57.8 kJ/mol $-$ [298 K $\times$ ($-$ $176 Jk^{-1}$ mol$^{-1})$]

= $-$57.8 kJ/mol $-$ $\left (298\times \frac{-176}{1000}kJ\right )$ [$\therefore$ 1 kJ = 1000 J]

= $-$ 5.352 kJ/mol

| $\Delta$G | = 5.352

Hence, answer is 5.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: The sum of oxidation states of two silver ions in [$Ag(NH_{3})_{2}$] [$Ag(CN)_{2}$] complex is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{2}][\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{2}]$ is made of the complex cation $[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{2}]{}^{+}$ and the complex anion $[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{2}]{}^{-}$.

In $[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{2}]{}^{+}$, $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is a neutral ligand: $x+2(0)=+1\Rightarrow x=+1$.

In $[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{2}]{}^{-}$, each $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ carries $-1$: $x+2(-1)=-1\Rightarrow x=+1$.

Sum of the oxidation states of the two silver ions $=(+1)+(+1)=2$.

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text:
The number of atoms in 8g of sodium is x $\times$ $10^{23}$. The value of x is $____________. ($Nearest integer)

[Given : $N_{A} = 6.02$ $\times$ $10^{23}$ mol$^{-1}$

Atomic mass of Na = 23.0 u]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, mass of Na = 8g

Molar mass of Na = 23 gmol$^{-1}$

$\frac{Weightofsodiumatom}{Molecularmassofsodiumatom}=\frac{Numberofatoms}{Avogadro^{'}snumber}$

$\frac{8g}{23g}=\frac{Numberofatoms}{6.022\times 10^{23}}$

Number of atoms $=\frac{8\times 6.022}{23}\times 10^{23}$

Number of atoms = 2.09 $\times$ $10^{23}$

x $\approx$ 2

Hence, answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text:
If 80 g of copper sulphate CuSO$_{4} . 5H_{2}O$ is dissolved in deionised water to make 5L of solution. The concentration of the copper sulphate solution is x $\times$ $10^{-3}$ mol $L^{-1}$. The value of x is $_____________$.

[Atomic masses Cu : 63.54u, S : 32u, O : 16u, H : 1u]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, mass of CuSO$_{4} . 5H_{2}O = 80 g$

The concentration of copper sulphate solution is x $\times$ $10^{-3}$ mol/L.

Molarity = $\frac{Numberofmolesofsolute}{Volumeofsolution(L)}$ ..... (i)

Molar mass of CuSO$_{4} . 5H_{2}O = 63.54 + 32 + 16$ $\times$ 4

 = 5 $\times$ 18 = 249.54 g/mol

Number of moles of solute = $\frac{Weightofsolute}{Molecularmassofsolute}$

= $\frac{80g}{249.54g/mol}$ = 0.32 mol

Volume of solution = 5 L

From Eq. (i),

Molarity = $\frac{0.3205}{5}$ = 64.11 $\times$ $10^{-3}$ mol/L

$\therefore$ x = 64.11

or x $\approx$ 64

Hence, answer is 64.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: A 50 watt bulb emits monochromatic red light of wavelength of 795 nm. The number of photons emitted per second by the bulb is x $\times$ $10^{20}$. The value of x is $__________$. [Given : h = 6.63 $\times$ $10^{-34} Js$ and c = 3.0 $\times$ $10^{8} ms^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Energy of one photon:

$E=\dfrac{hc}{λ}=\dfrac{6.63\times 10^{-34}\times 3.0\times 10^{8}}{795\times 10^{-9}}=2.50\times 10^{-19}\text{J}$

A 50 W bulb emits $50\text{J}$ of energy every second, so the number of photons emitted per second is

$n=\dfrac{50\text{J s}^{-1}}{2.50\times 10^{-19}\text{J}}\approx 2.0\times 10^{20}\text{s}^{-1}$

So $x=2$.

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: If the conductivity of mercury at 0${}^{\circ }$C is 1.07 $\times$ $10^{6} S m^{-1}$ and the resistance of a cell containing mercury is 0.243$\Omega$, then the cell constant of the cell is x $\times$ $10^{4} m^{-1}$. The value of x is $____________. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Conductance (G) is reciprocal of resistance (R)

$R=\frac{1}{G}$ or $G=\frac{1}{R}=\frac{1}{0.243\Omega }=4.115\Omega ^{-1}$

Relation between conductance (G),

conductivity ($κ$) and cell constant $\left (\frac{l}{A}\right )$ is given as

$κ=\frac{Gl}{A}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{l}{A}=\frac{κ}{G}=\frac{1.07\times 10^{6}Sm^{-1}}{4.115\Omega ^{-1}}=26\times 10^{4}m^{-1}\Rightarrow x=26$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift
